entries.en: I've had enough of this place.
I'm ready to move on.
Yeah?
Shepard.
What is it?
I'm ready.
This place has seen better days.
Let's go.
Ready when you are.
Where to?
I hate the cold.
So this is where Saren's been hiding.
Those salarians were tougher than I expected.
Damn geth are everywhere.
Strange place.
I'm coming.
Saren's close. I can feel it.
We've almost got him.
Stealing an Alliance ship. Risky stuff.
But I'm right behind you, Shepard. It's the least I can do.
No sign of pursuit. That's good.
Shepard. What can I do for you?
Nice ship you've got, Shepard.
What can I do for you?
There's no story.
Go ask the quarian if you want stories.
Well, there was this one time the turians almost wiped out our entire race. That was fun.
It's not the same.
So your people were infected with a genetic mutation?
An infection that makes only a few in a thousand children survive birth?
And I suppose it's destroying your entire species?
I don't expect you to understand, but don't compare humanity's fate with the krogan.
Your ignorance doesn't upset me, Shepard.
As for the krogan, I gave up on them long ago.
The genophage infected us, but it's not what's killing us.
Ask the salarians if you want details. They made it.
Every krogan is infected. Every one. And no one's rushing to find a cure.
When was the last time you saw a krogan scientist?
It's just who we are, Shepard. I can't change that. Nobody can.
We're sure not getting any stronger.
We're too spread out. None of us are interested in staying in our own system.
But they go to colonize new worlds.
We're not settlers. We're warriors. We want to fight.
So we leave. Hire ourselves out. And most of us never go back.
Shepard.
What do you want, Shepard?
Lots of reasons.
Such as... I needed to get out of our system. I needed to eat. I needed to survive.
I tried to help. That's why I had to leave.
I was head of a small tribe. We were trying to restore order after the war, but the other tribes were against us.
He wanted to continue the war. He wanted us to fight: turians, salarians, each other. It didn't matter who as long as we were fighting.
I just wanted Jarrod to shut up. To stop his ranting. I wanted him to stop leading the tribes astray. But he couldn't understand how much things had changed.
We didn't have the numbers to go to war. Even if we did, the genophage made sure we couldn't replenish our numbers fast enough.
And for a while, we were getting through. Some of the tribes started coming around.
No. He didn't. He arranged a Crush with the tribes. A meeting on neutral ground. He wanted to talk.
Shepard.
Never a dull moment with you, Shepard.
Commander. Things got heated back on Virmire...
Shepard.
So long, Wrex.
What's your story, Wrex?
You krogan live for centuries. Don't tell me you haven't had a few interesting adventures.
They tried the same with us. But we fought them off.
I heard about that. You know, they almost did the same to us.
It seems similar enough to me.
I suppose it isn't all the same.
You're still here. It can't be all that bad.
Sorry, Wrex. I wasn't trying to get you upset.
I was just making conversation. I wasn't trying to upset you.
What can you tell me about the genophage?
Why don't the krogan try to find a cure?
Are your people really dying?
Lots of species have left their homes and prospered.
So long, Wrex.
Why did you become a mercenary?
Such as?
Why not stay and help your people?
What did you want?
I take it the warlord didn't appreciate that.
Wrex.
Goodbye.
Personal inquiry.
Come on.
Just a short one.
Don't be an ass.
Big deal.
Yeah.
That's unfortunate.
Of course it is.
Sure it is.
Not exactly.
I see your point.
So what?
I won't.
Touchy subject?
Genophage
Extinction
I see.
What?
So?
Personal inquiry
Like?
Elaborate.
Yes?
Why leave?
What about you?
And....
What about Jarrod?
Goodbye.
I hope you know what you're doing, Shepard.
Sometimes crazy is the best way to go.
I just hope they don't catch us before we get our hands on Saren.
You'll get us through, Shepard.
I'd just hate to get stopped now.
With you, anything's possible.
I hope you're right.
You did what you had to do. I respect your choice.
It wasn't an easy choice. Don't make me regret it.
That... is why I left. And that's why I'll never go back.
Long enough. I took my first contract right after I left my home system.
It's good work if it doesn't kill you.
Sure. You get to see the galaxy on someone else's credits and most days end with a good fight.
I've tried more organized fighting. Private armies and such. But it gets too messy.
I fight best on my own. Or in very small groups. I don't like people relying on me, and I bloody well don't like relying on them.
I'm a fighter. It's what I do.
What the hell do you want me to do about it, Shepard?
I'm tired of sticking my ass on the line and getting nothing for it.
I decided killing for credits was better than killing for a lost cause.
I gave up on fighting for a lost cause.
I'm not like you, Shepard. I'm no hero.
I'm no hero, Shepard.
Bottom line: killing for credits simplifies things.
But there's a lot of krogan mercs out there. I'm always running into them.
Half the time I'm being paid to kill them. But that's just part of the job. You don't get to pick who your enemies are.
You trying to make me cry, Shepard?
I've got some unfinished business with my family. But that's all.
[sigh] Before I left, I made an oath to my father's father.
I swore to recover my family's battle armor. It was taken from him after the uprising.
It's a relic; useless, really. But it was worn by five generations of my family before the war. It's rightfully mine.
Saving the galaxy from certain destruction? No.
But I've had my share of adventures.
A few. I remember one time I was hired by a volus diplomat.
What an ass.
He wanted me to erase his past. Get rid of an old friend who knew too much.
Huh. His "old friend" turned out to be an asari commando.
What? No. Aleena and I were old friends. Sort of.
Anyway. When I told Aleena about the diplomat's contract, she and I had a good laugh about it.
Well, I wasn't going to lose the contract, but I respected Aleena. In the end, I let her pick the location where we'd fight.
Then, just when I thought I had her, the station's core went critical. Barely made it back to my ship in time.
I watched the station from a distance. I never saw her leave. And when that place blew... there was nothing left larger than a turian's right nut.
Aleena was still alive, and she was really pissed.
Easiest job I ever had. A little boring, but credits are credits.
Everyone else thinks I'm crazy.
You think I'm crazy, don't you?
I'm not as crazy as everyone thinks.
You and me both.
They won't.
I appreciate what you did, Wrex. I won't forget it.
Don't make me regret letting you live.
How long have you been a merc?
I get the feeling you enjoy your work.
So you'd rather be a merc than help your people?
Aren't you at all worried about what will happen to the krogan?
So you decided to go your own way.
So you're just giving up on your people?
Exactly. That's why I hired you.
You ever think about helping your people?
You must have family other than your father. Don't you miss them?
What kind of business?
What's so important about this armor?
You ever go an any missions like ours before?
Do you remember any that stick out?
I can see why that might give you pause.
So what did you do?
I assume the asari commando didn't make it.
What about the diplomat? He wanted her dead.
I won't.
Don't worry.
Same to you.
Mercenary.
You like it, then?
Personal inquiry.
So?
I see.
Don't blame you.
That's your reason?
I suppose.
Smart.
Sometimes.
Family
Go on.
Get to the point.
Really?
Armor
Personal inquiry.
Adventures.
Ouch.
Then what?
Close call.
And the volus?
Good.
Thanks.
Just say it.
You too?
Have some faith.
Don't worry.
Trust me.
No kidding.
Don't worry.
Just make sure it was worth it.
Saren has to pay for what he's done.
He'll do more than just answer if I have anything to say about it.
I could tell as soon as I met him.
I would've if I'd thought it was important.
This was a while ago. A bunch of mercs were bragging about a job out near the edges of the Terminus Systems.
They said it paid well and the boss was never around to ride them.
They said he was looking for more men, too. So, I checked it out.
It wasn't that open. And he only showed his face once.
I had a really bad feeling about him, so I got the hell out. Didn't even wait to get paid.
It was a volus trading vessel. Big one, lots of guards. But they were no match for us.
I don't know. All I saw on that ship was food and medical supplies. There were some basic weapons, but nothing big.
That's why I didn't mention it sooner.
Yeah. Didn't even know who he was. Still wouldn't if I hadn't joined up with you.
But my instincts were right.
Every other merc on that mission turned up dead within a week. Every damn one.
Let me see.
Damn, this is it. Hard to believe my ancestors wore this piece of crap. But at least it's back where it belongs.
Thanks, Shepard. I might be starting to like you after all.
Huh. Just 'cause I like you doesn't mean I wouldn't kill you.
Originally, it was taken by the turian military. We weren't allowed armor or weapons after the war.
He's got several bases where he stores his goods. All fortified and guarded. I just don't know which base has my family's armor.
I'll upload the data to your nav system. But, Commander, I want to be there when you find him.
No. Now that I have my family's armor again, there's nothing left for me.
That's what I expect from all my people.
We'll have him soon enough. Then he can answer for his crimes.
No matter what it takes, I'm going to hunt him down and kill him.
I don't really care, Wrex.
Why didn't you tell me this sooner?
I think I'd like to hear about it just the same.
I'll decide what's important. Now tell me how you know Saren.
I didn't know Saren was openly recruiting mercs.
Whose ship was it?
What kind of cargo was the freighter carrying? What was Saren after?
That's the only time you saw him?
I think I already found it, Wrex.
You getting soft on me, Wrex?
Who has it?
Just tell me where to start looking.
I found this armor. Does it belong to you?
Wrex, I think I found your armor.
I should hope so.
Good.
Thank you.
Agreed.
Yes
Oh, he will.
Goodbye.
You knew Saren?
Keep talking.
Fair enough.
That's my call.
Damn.
Saren recruited you?
Ship
Cargo
That's it?
I found it.
Where is it?
No problem.
I'll look for it.
Found something of yours.
Found your armor.
Got your back.
Right behind you.
I was betrayed.
And that's why I joined. So I wouldn't have to deal with them.
I try not to.
It seems pretty much the same to me.
What happened?
It isn't?
Really?
Interesting.
Good.
She chose some old salarian space station overrun with mercs and smugglers. That way we didn't have to worry about hurting any innocent bystanders.
I told him the truth.
I told him if he wanted to live, he'd need me around to protect him.
[laughs] He kept me on as his personal guard until he died. Natural causes.
Were you afraid of her?
You're smarter than you look, Wrex.
And he believed you?
Ah.
So?
Did Aleena get out?
But....
Cagey.
You told him that?
Suit yourself.
Colony's tougher than it looks.
The Thorian and the geth made a real mess here.
What do the geth want with this place?
What are we still doing here?
Nothing.
Goodbye.
I like the sound of that.
All I know: it makes breeding nearly impossible. Thousands die in stillbirth, and most never get that far.
You ask a krogan: would he rather find a cure for the genophage or fight for credits? He'll choose fighting every time.
So, we've got Saren on the run.
Good? He's rotten. To the core.
We'd been raiding ships in the area for months when we took out this massive cargo freighter. Our biggest haul yet.
I was on board checking bodies for valuables, looking for some extra credits. That's when I saw him.
Couple of the mercs called him by name, but he never spoke to them. Never spoke to anyone.
If there was anything of value on that ship, I didn't see it.
We met at the Hollows, near the graves of our ancestors. The skulls of our dead laid bare to remind us where we come from, and where we all go.
It's as sacred as any krogan place can be. Violence is forbidden.
I did. But when your father invites you to a Crush... well, there are some laws even we hold sacred.
He was. Until that day.
We talked. But we didn't get anywhere. When it was clear that I wouldn't join him, he gave the signal.
I escaped with my life. But not before I sank my dagger deep into my father's chest.
Now, it's in the hands of Tonn Actus. A turian scum who collects relics from the war. He's made millions selling krogan artifacts that were stolen from my people.
We met when we were both contracted to kill the same turian. Neither of us wanted the other one to get him first.
We spent more time fighting each other than tracking that turian.
It was a tie.
I brought back his head; she got the rest of him. As far as I know, we both got paid.
Huh. She was always a bit of a softy.
What didn't happen? For two days, I chased her through that station. Used my entire store of ammunition. Had to kill a bunch of mercs and use their crap weapons.
She'd locked herself in the medlabs. She was trying to patch herself up. Damn tough, that one.
It won't be long now. Saren's good, but I'm better.
It sounds like a trap to me. You must've suspected as much.
Jarrod was your father?
I guess even politicians have need of mercs from time to time, huh?
Which one of you made it first?
What happened on the station?
Yes we do.
That's risky.
And you went?
Your father?
Volus Diplomat?
Who got him?
Good bye.
Go on.
I don't know what he wanted. He was just moving through the ship. Watching.
They followed Jarrod, one of the few warlords who survived the war with the turians.  But he was old, and so were his ideas.
So, I headed back to the diplomat to give him the good news and collect my pay. But before I got halfway there, Aleena sent me a message: "Better luck next time."
Now, I'm not superstitious, but if someone can survive that, well... they deserve to live. At least for a bit longer.
What did Saren want with the ship?
What was he doing?
What bout the fight?
I told them all to forget about war. We needed to focus on breeding. At least for one generation.
His men leapt from the graves of our ancestors like krogan undead! The few that were loyal to me died quickly.
I already told you, Shepard. I promised to find my family's armor. Other than that, there's nothing left for me there.
By the third day, the station was barely holding together. The mercs were dead or gone, life support was failing. But I had her.
What?
I wouldn't say it's unusual. Mercs come in all shapes.
An asari commando mercenary? That's unusual, isn't it?
She was a merc?
Time to time? If it wasn't for politicians, I'd be out of work. They're always looking for ways to get ahead. This one was no different.
What did he want you to do?
What was the job?
You didn't kill her?
Have it your way.
Citadel
We should keep moving.
I'm looking forward to getting off this station.
Commander.
Yes?
Right behind you.
Got your back, Commander.
Feros
This place is a mess.
I can't believe the colony held out as long as it did.
Ready when you are.
Moving out.
Noveria
I've never seen so much ice and snow.
Strange place for the geth to show up.
I'm with you, Commander.
Virmire
Saren's here somewhere. I can feel it.
There's something about this place.
Ilos
What is this place?
I keep feeling like someone's watching us.
Endgame
Saren can't run forever.
We've almost got him.
I can't believe we stole the Normandy.
After everything you told me... It seems a bit extreme, don't you think?
I mean, I'm not surprised after everything you've told me. But still....
It's risky, but hopefully it'll pay off.
Well, it looks like we're free and clear. So far.
Commander. Nice work out there.
Thanks for bringing me on board, Commander.
Commander. Good to see you.
Well, not as much as you. But yeah, I've seen some interesting things.
I remember this salarian geneticist I was sent to investigate.
Commander. I... What can I do for you?
It's Saren. I'm starting to wonder whether we'll ever find him.
He's always one step ahead of us. And he's got those damn geth....
Commander. I wanted to thank you.
Shepard.
You've been with C-Sec a while. Have you seen much action?
I bet you have. Anything in particular that stands out?
Something bothering you?
Personal questions
Anything specific?
What's the matter?
Where to next, Commander?
Awaiting orders.
Ready and waiting.
I knew working with a Spectre would be better than life at C-Sec.
Well, no. But I know what they're like.
Spectres make their own rules. You're free to handle things your way.
At C-Sec, you're buried by rules. The damn bureaucrats are always on your back.
Exactly my point.
Maybe. But sometimes it feels like the rules are only there to stop me from doing my work.
If I'm trying to take down a suspect, it shouldn't matter how I do it, as long as I do it.
But C-Sec wants it done their way. Protocol and procedure come first. That's why I left.
It didn't start out bad, but as I rose in ranks, I got saddled with more and more red tape.
And without C-Sec headquarters looking over my shoulder, well, maybe I can get the job done my way for a change.
I wasn't trying to-- I understand, Commander.
Thank you, Commander.
Don't worry, Commander. I'll keep clear.
Have you worked with a Spectre before?
Being a Spectre does have its advantages.
For the most part, the rules are there for a reason.
If getting the job done means endangering innocent people, then, no. We get the job done right, not fast. Got it?
As long as you do your job well, you're free to go about your business as you see fit.
Just do a good job and don't get in my way. We'll get along fine.
You knew?
You shouldn't complain.
True.
It's not that bad.
That depends.
Sounds good to me.
Whatever.
He despises the Spectres. He hates the idea of someone having unlimited power with no accountability. He wouldn't like you, Commander. No offense.
That case was a bit... disturbing.
Spoken like a true C-Sec officer.
I suppose I can understand his concern.
Not all Spectres are like Saren, you know.
Typical.
I see.
Too bad.
I was tasked with tracking black market trade on the Citadel. Most of it's harmless. Nothing I needed to pursue.
But during the course of my investigation, I noticed an increase in the trade of body parts. Organs, mostly.
We usually get a few of those, but not the numbers I was seeing. We weren't sure if there was a new black market lab or if some freak was harvesting organs from citizens.
Both, actually. But it took us a while to figure that out.
First, we got a hold of a sample and ran DNA tests. The weird thing was, the match led us to a turian who was still alive and was very convinced he'd never lost his liver.
So I went to his lab, hoping to find evidence of cloned organ development. But there was nothing. No salarian hearts, no turian livers, not one krogan testicle.
Some krogan believe that testicle transplants can increase their virility. Counteract the effects of the genophage.
It doesn't work, but that doesn't stop them from buying. They'll pay up to 10,000 credits each. That's 40,000 for a full set.
Somebody's making a killing out there.
I brought in some of his employees for interrogation. To see if I could get them to talk.
While I was interviewing one of them, I came across something suspicious.
Exactly. Though in this case, it paid off in a different way.
Maybe. Maybe not. Either way, it paid off.
One of my detainees started bleeding profusely during the interview. We offered to patch him up and he got frantic. Freaked out.
I ordered a full exam, to find out what was going on. Our medics found incisions all over his body. Some of them fresh.
That was our big break. These people weren't just Dr. Saleon's employees. They were test tubes. Walking, living test tubes.
Exactly. He cloned their organs right inside their own bodies. Then he harvested them and sold them off.
Most of the victims were poor. He'd pay them each a small percentage of the sales, but only if the organs were good.
He ran. Blew his lab, grabbed some of his employees, and headed for the nearest space dock.
By the time I found out, his ship was already leaving. He threatened to kill his hostages if we tried to stop him.
I ordered Citadel defense to shoot him down, but C-Sec headquarters countermanded my order.
I told them those hostages were dead anyway. He'd just use them to make more organs. But they wouldn't listen.
No. But letting him get away like that....
They sent the military after him, but he got away just the same.
Yes, they did. I went to Pallin and told him what I thought of him and his policies. He said if I didn't like it, I could quit. I almost did.
All they had to do was disable that ship. Stop him from running. Maybe the hostages die, maybe they don't. But at least we stop the bastard responsible for it all.
Yeah. Maybe you're right. It doesn't make it any easier, but I see your point.
Yeah. Exactly. I mean, those hostages might be wishing they'd died by now anyway.
I suppose. Can't waste too much time worrying about it now.
I wish I had your confidence. I just can't stand the thought of him getting away with everything he's done.
I know you're doing everything you can. And if anyone can catch him, it's you, but...
If there's anything else I can do to help. Anything. Just tell me what you want me to do and I'll do it.
Yes, sir. I'll be ready.
Yes, ma'am. You can count on me.
Can I ask you something, Commander?
I mean, they were really dragging their heels before. What if we find him, bring him back to the Citadel, and they refuse to act?
Well, maybe we shouldn't give them the chance, Commander.
In my opinion, Saren's too dangerous to be kept alive. Too much could happen. He could escape, or the Council might let him go....
If we find him-- when we find him. I say we make sure we stop him. Permanently.
Fair enough. Either way, I'm right behind you, Commander.
But what's the point in keeping him alive? It just gives him an opportunity to escape or convince the Council to listen to him.
And what about the geth? They might try to free him!
Yeah. I see your point. Do you really think there's more to know? Other than the fact he's a raving lunatic?
Yes, sir.
Yes, ma'am.
Good. The Council won't like it, but they can't stop you, either.
You see, this is why I want to be a Spectre.
You never have to worry about bureaucratic idiots making a mess of everything.
What happened? Why were you investigating him?
So what was it?
So how did you figure out what was happening?
You're kidding, right? Why would anyone want krogan testicles?
What did you do about the geneticist?
Yeah. Go on.
Good thinking. Lackeys are always easier to scare.
You mean threatening. Was that really necessary?
So he was growing spare parts in his own employees.
He was growing parts inside these people?
Why not? What the hell happened?
But you went after him anyway, right?
Well, you can't get them all.
It's not worth the risk. You pursue the vessel and disable it. That's the best choice.
No wonder you hated it there. Those idiots just let him fly away.
If you don't care about the fate of those hostages, then you're no better than he is. You're just a terrorist with a badge.
A few casualties is a small price to pay to stop someone like that.
I suppose I can see both sides. But what's done is done.
We're getting close, Garrus. We'll find him.
I understand your concern, but we will find him. Just make sure you're ready to go when we do.
Thank you, Garrus. I'll keep that in mind. Just make sure you're ready to go when we do catch him.
What is it?
I get the feeling this isn't a question. Speak your mind, Garrus.
You seem to have some thoughts on this. Speak your mind, Garrus.
It'll depend on the situation. I'm not committing to anything until I've got him in my sights.
If Saren won't listen to reason, if he forces my hand, I'll kill him in a heartbeat. But only if it's absolutely necessary.
We know more about Saren's plans than anyone, but what do we really know? If we just kill him, we lose the chance to find out.
Maybe, maybe not. But it's not a chance I'm willing to take.
This isn't up for debate, Garrus. Now fall in line!
I'm glad you see it that way. I never had any intention of capturing that bastard. When I see him, he dies.
Just make sure you're ready when it happens.
Disturbing?
How so?
Really?
What did you find?
Krogan testicles.
So.
What about the doctor?
What?
Smart.
Interviewing?
Test tubes?
Interesting.
That's sick.
What?
What?
I see.
I agree with them.
Idiots!
You're wrong.
You're right.
Tough choice.
You think he'll get away?
Are you worried?
All right.
Of course.
What are you saying?
It's possible.
We'll see.
Last resort.
Agreed.
Use your head.
Think about it!
Enough!
I don't know.
Dismissed.
Yes, Commander.
After a bit of digging, I discovered this turian worked briefly for Dr. Saleon, the geneticist.
Sometimes an organ wouldn't grow properly, so he'd just leave it in them. Most of them were a mess, but only on the inside -- hidden so nobody could see it.
That's the worst part. We never caught him.
They were worried about the hostages. Worried about civilian casualties if the ship was destroyed so close to the Citadel.
I realized it wasn't because of what he did to those people. That was part of it. But I think most of it was because he got away from me.
He escaped under my watch, and I didn't like that. I let it become personal.
This way, we'll know he'll never hurt anyone again.
For everything. Taking me with you. Letting me be part of your team. I've learned a lot.
I'm, uh... Thanks, Commander.
I've thought a lot about what you said. About eliminating the threat immediately. Regardless of the cost. You were right.
I always knew C-Sec's methods were flawed, but it's more than that. I can see now just how dangerous that type of thinking can be.
I've thought a lot about what you've told me. About not sacrificing innocents to achieve the goal. About finding the best way through, not just the fastest.
I still think C-Sec has its flaws, but I understand why they do it now. I see the importance of being firm in the face of evil. Not letting it change who I am.
Don't worry, Commander. I will.
If the people I'm sworn to protect can't trust me... well, then I don't deserve to be the one protecting them.
Stealing the Normandy is a trivial risk compared to the threat of Saren.
We'll be fine, Garrus. Just be ready when we find Saren.
You sound worried, Garrus.
I hope he got what he deserved.
What for, Garrus?
You're welcome, Garrus.
I'm glad you see it that way. Keep that in mind when we meet Saren.
Words mean nothing until you turn them into action, Garrus. What are you going to do about it?
What choice did we have?
So long.
Scared?
Did you interview him?
Bastard.
They just let him go?
Thank me?
Sure.
Very good.
Is that it?
Yeah, I suppose you're right.
No, not really.
If you're wrong, we'll pay for it. But if you're right, and we did nothing, I think we'd regret it a whole lot more.
I just hope we can catch Saren before they realize we're missing.
Oh. Goodbye, Commander.
Commander.
Every so often, some lab sells unwanted parts through the black market. But they're not as bad as the psychos.
I remember this one elcor diplomat we caught in my first year on the job. He was hacking people up and selling their organs. Had the station in a bit of a panic.
But this case wasn't that clear cut. Turns out there was more going on than we first realized.
I just wish I could have stopped him. That's all.
